solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Guitar piece that makes one experience anxiety

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the raised ridges across a guitar's fingerboard
second meaning: to worry or be agitated

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated meanings of one short word; 'that makes one' simply joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a ridge on a stringed instrument's neck, and the verb means to worry anxiously.

clue.text: Boundaries set up by male — that's unfair to females

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: the thing that treats women unfairly

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it, so the boundaries word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: in cricket a six is a boundary hit clearing the rope without bouncing

explanation.surface: A man rigs the scoring so that the boundaries count against the women's team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a six is the biggest kind of boundary hit, so boundaries are sixes; reversed upwards, then male is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexism is prejudice or discrimination on the basis of sex, typically against women.

clue.text: One positive response, or more than one

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a plural: several of the votes just described

parts.note: a means one, as in a single item
yes is the affirmative answer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a single yes counts, or whether several are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: a yes is one positive response, and the answer is more than one of them, as votes are counted.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliamentary voting the ayes are the votes cast in favour, so plural affirmatives.

clue.text: In time, informer making things wrong in work

indicators.note: the informer is placed in the word for time, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is slang for someone who betrays others to the authorities

explanation.surface: Over time, a snitch at the office ends up making mistakes in the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are the list of errors found in a printed book, so mistakes in a published work.

clue.text: Loud singer including sequence of songs in high voice

indicators.note: the singer's word takes the song sequence inside it

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
a set is a group of songs a band performs in one go

explanation.surface: A loud vocalist runs through a set list while singing in a high register.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificially high vocal register that male singers use above their normal range.

clue.text: Unlike readers, the writer will perform repeatedly

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves says I'll, the contraction of I will
to iterate is to repeat an action again and again

explanation.surface: An author promises to keep doing something over and over, quite unlike the people who read the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter, so I; with 'will' that gives I'LL, apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot read is the opposite of a reader, which is what the clue's negative definition captures.

clue.text: Warm kind of fire that's a contradiction in terms?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: kindly and welcoming in manner

definitions.text: kind of fire that's a contradiction in terms?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: ... fire, being shot by one's own side, which is hardly ...

explanation.walkthrough: Friendly fire is accidental attack by one's own forces; the question mark flags that such fire is anything but kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm person is affable and approachable, and military fire from allies is called by the same adjective.

clue.text: Movement in no hurry to follow left-winger

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
Trot is short for a Trotskyist, a far-left radical

explanation.surface: A slow march trails behind a radical socialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow' looks like it orders the pieces, but it is the verb meaning to shadow someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogtrot is a gentle, easy-paced run, the gait of an unhurried animal.

clue.text: Make a recovery without drug, in fact

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside: the recovery word goes outside the drug

parts.note: to rally is to recover strength or rise again after a fall
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone gets better without taking any medicine, which is genuinely the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean lacking, but here it means outside, so the drug goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Really is an adverb meaning actually or in truth, just as the phrase does.

clue.text: Carefully planned operation catching ringleader for part of racket

indicators.note: the police operation traps the leader inside it

parts.note: a sting is an elaborate undercover deception to catch criminals
the leader, or first letter, of ring

explanation.surface: A police sting nets the boss of a criminal racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests crime, but it is the sports bat whose strings are woven across the frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis racket's face is strung with tight cords, each one a piece of the whole racket.

clue.text: Close family wrapping son in fur

indicators.note: the two words for close and family surround the son, who sits between them

parts.note: to seal is to close firmly
kin means relatives

explanation.surface: Relatives close by swaddle a baby boy in fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealskin is the pelt of a seal, prized as a fur for coats.

clue.text: Good ensemble in dance performance, mainly in royal residence

indicators.note: the good and ensemble words go inside the dance word
most of the word, so the performance loses its last letter

parts.note: a ballet is a theatrical dance performance
moral means good or virtuous
a cast is the ensemble of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A virtuous company performs in a ballet staged at a royal home.
explanation.walkthrough: BALLET without its final T gives BALLE, which is split around the other two pieces. Balmoral Castle is the British royal family's estate in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle in Aberdeenshire is a private Scottish home of the British monarch.

clue.text: Preparing to fight with friend outside, in scary fashion

indicators.note: the friend word sits outside, wrapped round the preparation word

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter
arming is equipping oneself with weapons for battle

explanation.surface: Taking up weapons alongside a friend looks frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes something done in a frightening, worrying manner.

clue.text: Unsociable type's side-splitting joke?

indicators.note: the joke word divides the side letters, sitting between them

parts.note: a side can be left or right, abbreviated L and R, the two letters taken here
a joke is a one, as in have you heard the one about

explanation.surface: A solitary man tells a gag that has everyone in fits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side-splitting' reads as hilarious, but it is a side being split, left and right, by the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner is a person who prefers solitude and avoids company.

clue.text: Like Northern people as part of race, you might say

indicators.note: spoken aloud the word is heard rather than spelt, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a racetrack

explanation.surface: A runner compares northern folk to one stage of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Lapp is the older name for the Sami of northern Scandinavia, now often considered dated.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means relating to the Sami people of Arctic Lapland.

clue.text: Weapon the old man has for response to challenge

parts.note: old man is informal for father, so pa
the 's contraction of has, as in pa's got
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: Father owns a sword, ready for any challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Challenge' suggests a duel, but it is a sentry's demand to identify oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A password is the secret word given in reply to a sentry's challenge.

clue.text: One century after another — that'll make you feel better

indicators.note: the one and the century come after the other century in the answer

parts.note: another century, here the slang ton for a hundred
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A batsman scores one hundred after another, which lifts the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Both TON and C mean a hundred; 'another' points back to century for its meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a restorative medicine or anything invigorating that lifts one's mood.

clue.text: Company custom to maintain an intimate in-house relationship

parts.note: a habit is a customary practice

explanation.surface: Business tradition seems to be keeping an office romance going.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohabit is to live together as a couple without being married.

clue.text: Love to talk back? That's fine

parts.note: a zero score in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: talking back here means the chatter word is read backwards

parts.note: to yak is to chatter at length

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether answering a loved one back is acceptable, and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay is an informal expression of approval or agreement, meaning all right.

clue.text: Put right about wrong I, perhaps, interpreted incorrectly

indicators.note: the repaired word goes round the reworked letters

parts.note: mended means repaired
taken as written

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put in a wrong order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone corrected a misreading, perhaps of the pronoun I.
explanation.walkthrough: MENDED splits after M to take the eight letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To misapprehend is to misunderstand, so this past form means misunderstood.

clue.text: Balance I established within political group

indicators.note: set up inside, so the letter goes inside the group word

parts.note: a party is an organised political group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A member claims to keep things even inside the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity means equality or equivalence, a state of balance between two things.

clue.text: New and unusual editor signed agreement

parts.note: odd means strange or out of the ordinary

explanation.surface: A fresh and peculiar editor put their name to a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signed' suggests writing a name, but it means made a sign, a nod of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding is a gesture of assent, so to nod is to signal yes without words.

clue.text: Bloomer as second doctor comes in immediately before operation

indicators.note: the doctor enters the other pieces, standing between them
immediately sits ahead of the operation in the answer

parts.note: now means at once

explanation.surface: A doctor arrives just before surgery, a second too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is a flower that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a small white flowering plant, one of the first to bloom in late winter.

clue.text: Report about mass or ceremony

indicators.note: the report word goes round the letter for mass

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, or pop

explanation.surface: A news item about a church mass or another rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' suggests news, but here it is a gunshot-like bang.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is splendid ceremonial display, as in pomp and circumstance.

clue.text: Confused situation produced by strike on base

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a bed is a foundation or base layer
to lam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: Industrial action at a base leads to chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout, but it is the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam means uproar or chaos, named after a notorious London asylum.

clue.text: A border that's said to require attention

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an interjection: the sound uttered to get notice

parts.note: taken as written
a hem is the folded edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A trimmed edge, apparently, needs looking at.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is a small throat-clearing sound people make to attract notice or signal mild disapproval.

clue.text: Instrument that's dropped in red wine

indicators.note: the little word in is let fall out of the instrument

parts.note: the clarinet is a woodwind instrument
the word in, taken as written, is what is removed

explanation.surface: A musical instrument has been dropped into a glass of red.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'in' as a preposition, but it is the very letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Maiden spoke and spoke, in barely audible way

parts.note: uttered means spoke or voiced

explanation.surface: A young woman spoke on and on, but very quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: M for maiden is a cricket convention: a maiden over is one with no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutter is to speak quietly and indistinctly, often in complaint.
